sheets.prompt:
Four-panel character reference sheet following the reference layout: three full-body views (front / side / back) left to right, and one large head-and-shoulders close-up filling the right column; the exact same character, outfit and proportions in every panel; plain background. The first reference image is only the panel layout guide: copy its four-panel arrangement, not its grey mannequin shapes. Panel 1 (left): full-body front view, standing in a neutral pose, arms relaxed at the sides. Panel 2: full-body true side profile. Panel 3: full-body back view. Panel 4 (tall right column): head-and-shoulders close-up, facing the camera, neutral expression, face clearly lit under the hat brim. Each full-body figure is drawn a little small inside its panel, complete from the top of the hat to the soles of the boots with clear space above and below, standing on a small patch of plain floor with a soft contact shadow; if any part is cut off by the panel edge the sheet is wrong. Plain soft grey-green studio backdrop in every panel, even soft daylight, no scenery, no captions or labels.

Subject: Pat, an Irish farm labourer, a man about 35 years old, a real human actor, an ordinary working man with no caricature. Wiry and strong-armed, slightly stooped from digging, about 171 cm tall. Weather-reddened, lined face with broad cheekbones and a stubbled jaw; blue-grey eyes; shaggy, collar-length dark brown hair with short dark side-whiskers under the hat. Wary, reluctant, deferential demeanour. Wearing: a plain 1862 Irish farm labourer's working dress in earth tones: a collarless unbleached linen shirt with sleeves rolled up, a brown frieze wool waistcoat, patched brown corduroy trousers tied below the knee with string, heavy hobnailed boots and a battered brown soft felt hat; soil on the knees, worn and patched. Fresh garden soil also on his hands and boots. He holds a garden spade with a worn wooden D-handle, blade resting on the floor.

Style: Photorealistic live-action fantasy film rooted in England in 1862, shot on 35mm film with anamorphic lenses, 16:9 widescreen. Real sets, real locations and real costumed actors in 1862 dress. Wonderland spaces are real built sets and set extensions in an Alphonse Mucha-inspired Art Nouveau design: flowing organic lines, floral and vine ornament, circular halo roundels, mosaic and stained glass, aged pastel-and-gold surfaces with patina and moss; the waking 1862 meadow stays plain period realism. Talking animals and fantastical creatures are photoreal CGI animals with naturalistic anatomy, real fur, feathers, skin and scales, lit by the same light and grounded with real contact shadows. Natural and practical light: sunlight, candlelight and oil lamps, soft haze with volumetric light shafts and soft colour through stained glass. Restrained palette of verdigris teal, slate grey, dusty rose, soft sage and lilac pastels and tarnished-gold accents, warmed by amber sun and candle glow. Fine film grain, gentle halation, soft depth of field, grounded and quietly melancholy.
